summary: BMW executes 23 cache replays/frame. Complete-bin copies account for 7.472167% of replay input off, 10.125646% at 2x and 9.542854% at 4x; the remaining input passes through the captured depth-visibility filter. Every matching-angle counter row agrees across both audits. T-80 has zero cache replays in its 600 observed frames. All six quiet guards pass on the first attempt. Publication already swaps bin ownership, so there is no second publication copy to remove. The observations support evaluating visibility selection next; they establish no FPS gain or hardware limit.
interpretation: The unfiltered borrowing-only target covers a minority of observed BMW replay input and no T-80 replay. Full-bin copy shares are not CPU-time shares, and source ownership swaps do not prove zero physical cache traffic. Borrowing filtered data would require visibility traversal plus immutable lifetime protection. Instrumentation can affect coverage retirement scheduling; current diagnostic row equality does not establish a future uninstrumented performance gain.
nextResearchDirection: Evaluate stable visibility selection in aligned8-record bitmap groups: skip all-hidden groups, copy full-visible groups, enumerate mixed groups with native i32_ctz, bounded first/end groups and original record order. Keep existing owned arrays, clipping, depth-epoch conditions and queue protocol. Full regression and18paired off/2x/4x comparisons against current D4 required before adoption. This successor is not implemented or measured in this census.
